sections.h2: Which government bills a Cary home for property tax?
sections.html:
The county does, not the town. The Town of Cary says its limits now span three counties, Wake, Chatham and Durham, and that each county handles assessment, valuation, billing and collection for the town's tax.

Your parcel's location decides which of the three applies, and the bill itself or a county online search will tell you. The town page lists the numbers it wants residents to use:

  • Wake County Tax Administration, 919-856-5400. In-person help is at 301 S. McDowell St., Suite 3800, in Raleigh, weekdays from 8:30 in the morning to 5:00.
  • Chatham County Collection Division, 919-542-8250.
  • Durham County Tax Administrator, 919-560-0300.

Wake's page describes the arrangement: by local agreement the county sends the bills and collects the money for municipal and special districts within its borders. A Cary owner in Wake therefore pays one bill with the county and town rates together, and anyone with questions about how the town rate was set is told to ask the town. The town also adds a $30 vehicle license fee that rides on the vehicle tax bill, with no sticker.

sections.h2: What are the Cary and Wake County tax rates?
sections.html:
For fiscal year 2027 the official pages print 36.75 cents per $100 for the town and 53.71 cents per $100 for Wake County. Both are stated as printed on the official budget pages, and a bill adds the two when the parcel is in Wake.

The Cary Town Council adopted its budget at the regular meeting on June 25, 2026, raising the town rate by 2.75 cents. The same budget sets a solid waste and recycling fee of $28 per month, which is a town charge listed separately from the property tax rate. Wake's commissioners voted on June 1 for a 2-cent increase to reach 53.71 cents.

Both rates apply to the assessed value, so the value matters as much as the rate. Revaluation changes values, and the rate that follows can move in either direction. Chatham and Durham County parcels carry those counties' own rates, which you can get from the numbers above. Rates reset every July 1 with the budgets, so confirm them on the current bill instead of relying on last year's figure.

sections.h2: When are Cary property taxes due?
sections.html:
The due date is September 1, and a payment through January 5 owes nothing extra; interest begins January 6 under G.S. 105-360.

StepRuleSource
Listing periodFirst business day of January through January 31G.S. 105-307
Taxes dueSeptember 1G.S. 105-360
No interestThrough January 5G.S. 105-360 and Wake County
Interest charge2% for the stretch from January 6 to February 1, then three-fourths of a percent per monthG.S. 105-360
Relief applicationDeadline June 1, with late filing for good cause considered case by caseWake County

Wake lets owners make partial payments of any size without prior approval, provided the balance is paid by January 5, and it sends a statement with the remaining balance after each one. If your lender pays through escrow, no paper bill is mailed to you, and the online lookup shows the amount. Wake accepts ACH or eCheck, PayPal, Venmo, Apple Pay, Google Pay and the four major credit cards.

sections.h2: How does revaluation affect a Cary home's tax value?
sections.html:
Wake County reappraised on January 1, 2024, will do so again effective January 1, 2027, and has moved to a two-year cycle after that. State law only requires a reappraisal every eighth year, so Wake revalues far more often than the minimum.

Wake's page describes four steps: neighborhooding, land and building pricing from sales, field and office review, and the notice of assessment with appeal review. It divides about 460,000 parcels into 5,400 neighborhoods and builds a Schedule of Values that the Board of Commissioners must approve. The published schedule for the 2027 round shows results presented to the Board on January 19, 2027, value notices going out by January 22, 2027, and a planned appeal deadline of April 30, 2027.

A homeowner who disputes the notice takes the case to the county's review board. A loss at that board can go to the Property Tax Commission, with notice filed inside 30 days of the mailed decision, as G.S. 105-290 provides. For questions on the 2027 round, Wake runs a call center at 919-857-3800.

sections.h2: What tax relief is available to Cary homeowners?
sections.html:
Wake County administers three state programs for Cary owners in its portion: the Senior and Disabled Program, Tax Deferment and the Disabled Veteran Program. Wake's page says the programs reach low-income owners who are 65 or older, low-income owners who are 100% disabled, and veterans with total and permanent service-connected disability, along with unmarried surviving spouses.

  • Age or disability: $38,800 is the 2026 income limit, and a qualifying home loses whichever is more, $25,000 or half its appraised value, from the taxable amount.
  • Veterans: $45,000 of appraised value is excluded, and the state form sets no age or income test.
  • Circuit breaker: the bill is held to 4.0% of income, or to 5.0% when income runs past $38,800 and up to $58,200, after five years of owning and living in the home.

Wake says the deadline is June 1 under state law, and it considers late applications case by case for good cause through December 31 of that year. Forgetting or not knowing about a program is typically not good cause. Illness, a death in the immediate family, military deployment and delay in getting disability certification are the examples it gives. An owner gets one program, not a stack, so ask the tax office which one fits. See G.S. 105-277.1 for the exclusion rules.

sections.h2: What if I cannot pay my Cary property tax?
sections.html:
Call Wake County Tax Administration at 919-856-5400 before January 6. Wake says it can set up short-term payment plans, that earlier calls leave more options, and that it cannot help once a bill becomes overdue.

State law permits past due taxes to be taken from paychecks, bank accounts or rent, and the lien on the parcel is created by G.S. 105-355 as of the listing date. Foreclosure under G.S. 105-374 finishes with an auction at the courthouse door, though redemption remains possible before confirmation.

If a Cary house also has a mortgage in default, the tax lien and the lender's foreclosure can run at the same time, which narrows the timeline. A sale ahead of any auction leaves the price in the owner's hands, and closing pays the tax out of the proceeds.

sections.h2: What does Cary look like for a seller?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate for Cary is 183,582 people, a 5.0% climb from 174,787 in April 2020. It covers 59.23 square miles of land at 2,949.7 people per square mile.

  • Homes owned by their occupants are valued at a median $580,200 (2020-2024), and 66.6% of units are owner-occupied.
  • Gross rent has a median of $1,738.
  • Household income has a median of $134,905.
  • Foreign-born persons: 23.9%; bachelor's degree or higher: 70.5%.

The source for these is the Census Bureau QuickFacts page for Cary town. Check your value notice after each revaluation, since the assessed value is half of the tax calculation. Deeds are filed with the register of deeds of the county that holds the parcel. Wake's register states the excise tax at $2 per thousand dollars of price.

faqs.q: Which county do I pay Cary property tax to?
faqs.a: Pay the county that holds your parcel: Wake, Chatham or Durham. The Town of Cary says each of the three counties handles assessment, billing and collection for the town's tax, and Wake's page covers the parcels inside its borders.

faqs.q: What is the Cary town property tax rate?
faqs.a: The adopted fiscal year 2027 rate is 36.75 cents per $100 of assessed value, up 2.75 cents. Wake County's rate is 53.71 cents per $100, and Wake collects both for parcels in its portion.

faqs.q: When does Wake County interest begin on Cary taxes?
faqs.a: It starts on January 6, so a payment by January 5 escapes it. Then 2% applies until February 1, followed by three-fourths of a percent each month.

faqs.q: When is the next Wake County revaluation?
faqs.a: The next one takes effect January 1, 2027, and later ones follow every two years. Wake plans to start sending value notices by January 22, 2027.

faqs.q: Can a Cary senior reduce a property tax bill?
faqs.a: Possibly, if age or disability and income tests are met. The exclusion takes off $25,000 or half the value, whichever is larger, and Wake sets a June 1 deadline while weighing late filings for good cause.
